title: docs: document the unit-code backfill door (os migrate unit-codes and its REST twin) (follow-up of PR #35865)
body:
repo:objectstack#7 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibvMi1U7R2kBd3JbTPu

Filing gate: ③ an owed `Skills-docs:` follow-up, filed by the area thread before ACCEPT of PR #35865 (card #35492), per SKILL.md's `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` rule · Source: fleet

## What is owed

PR #35865 (Part of #35492, ADR-0158 R1) adds a maintenance door for stored unit text, and declares `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: added`:

- `os migrate unit-codes --object O --field F [--map-file FILE] [--org ID | --all-organizations] [--apply]`, which rewrites free-text units into unit codes from the operator's exact mapping. The dry run is the default, an apply over an unmapped value is refused before any write, and a second run writes nothing.
- Its tenant-admin twin `POST /api/v1/meta/_migrate-unit-codes`, behind `metadata.endpoints.maintenance` and `setup.write`, for the caller's organization only.
- Two new destructive-change findings, `unit_mode_to_record` and `unit_mode_to_code` (409 `DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE`, lifted by `force: true`), raised when a save declares a unit code field over stored rows. The unit write refusals now name the door as their remedy.

Who benefits: an operator or tenant admin who turns on units for an app that already holds free-text units ("kg", "pcs"). The refusal they meet names `os migrate unit-codes`, and today the docs say nothing about it. These pages do not mention it:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`: the `os migrate` table row and a section, beside `os migrate record-currency-codes` (line ~1532 and ~1861 on main);
- the `metadata.endpoints.maintenance` describe in `packages/spec/src/api/rest-server.zod.ts` and its generated `rest-server.mdx` (a describe edit ships bytes, so it takes a patch changeset);
- a units page under `content/docs/data-modeling/`, beside `currency.mdx`, that names the door (none exists yet; check the site structure and overlap with `field-types.mdx` first). The skill side of `unitConfig` is already #35808's row on #35769.

## Done when

- `cli.mdx` lists `os migrate unit-codes` in the migrate table and has a section with a dry-run and an apply example, the `""` entry for blanks, and the scope flags.
- The `maintenance` describe names the unit-code door beside the currency door, and the generated reference is regenerated.
- A data-modeling page (new, or a section of an existing one after the overlap check) explains converting stored units, and links the CLI section.
- It lands only after PR #35865 has merged, so the docs never name a door that main does not have.

Reader: the docs lane, set by triage. Blocked-by: #35492 (PR #35865).

Grading: area:data · Task · docs follow-up of an added CLI command and REST door · evidence: PR #35865 body and report 7041766952 (out_of_scope_findings); `git grep -n unit-codes origin/main -- content/docs` has no hit.
Suggested grade: p2 (an owed Skills-docs follow-up; the refusal names a door the docs do not describe). Small enough for the weekly sweep card if triage prefers.

Dedupe: `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue "unit-codes"` gives 19 hits; none is a docs card (the units cards #35339 #35404 #35469 #35488 #35489 #35492, plus unrelated currency and migrate cards).
